errors.description: The spanning tree does not necessarily index a directed system, so Lemma 3.6 cannot be applied as claimed. Orienting its edges upward can leave vertices with no common upper bound in the tree, even when the original poset is directed. For example, a directed poset with covers a,b < c,d < e can have a spanning tree containing a–c, b–c, a–d, c–e; in that tree c and d have no common upper bound. The construction therefore does not establish the claimed lim→f-simple module containing every f-simple.
errors.evidence: The proof asserts that assigning maps along the spanning tree “gives a directed system of f-simples” and then applies Lemma 3.6, which assumes a direct system. Acyclic orientation alone does not make an indexing category directed.
